title: Imaging Guiding panel: Dither is clickable with no guider connected and is a complete silent no-op
what_happened: Imaging -> Guiding tab with the guider Disconnected. The panel correctly warns 'No guider connected' and correctly greys out Start, but Stop and Dither render as active. I clicked Dither twice and screenshotted at +1.8 s (inside the snackbar window) and +5 s. No snackbar, no error banner, no log entry, no state change - nothing at all.
expected: Dither with no guider should either be disabled with the same treatment as Start, or say 'No guider connected - dither skipped'. Silence here is dangerous because dither-skipped is exactly the failure a user will not notice until stacking.
repro: 1. Leave the guider disconnected. 2. Imaging -> Guiding tab. 3. Click Dither. 4. Screenshot within 2 s; tail app.log.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-45-dither-fast.png (screenshot 1.8 s after the click - no snackbar anywhere), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-dither.png (panel shows 'No guider connected' yet Dither is active), app.log unchanged
proposed_fix: Gate Dither and Stop on guiderState.connectionState the way Start already is, and have the dither action report 'no guider' rather than returning silently.
verdict_reasoning: The observation reproduces: on Imaging -> Guiding with the guider Disconnected, the panel shows 'No guider connected', Start is visibly greyed, and Stop/Dither are drawn at full contrast with normal borders. I clicked Dither and screenshotted at ~2 s: no snackbar, no error banner, no state change, and the app log stayed at 1148 lines. But the proposed root cause is wrong — Dither and Stop ARE already gated: guiding_panel.dart:299 `isEnabled: isConnected && isGuiding && !_isDithering` and :283 `isEnabled: isConnected && isGuiding`. So nothing is ungated and no dither is ever silently skipped; what differs is that Start uses a button variant with a visible disabled treatment while Stop/Dither use one without, inside the same card. Same underlying defect class as the Guiding-screen finding (weak/inconsistent disabled affordance), so I am flagging it as a duplicate in mechanism, and reducing to P3 since there is no risk of an actually-skipped dither.

title: Guiding "Brain Settings" expands into skeleton placeholders that never resolve and never error
what_happened: With PHD2 disconnected I pressed 'Brain Settings' on the Guiding screen. The panel expanded into six grey shimmer/skeleton rows. 20 s later they were still shimmer rows: no values, no 'PHD2 not connected' message, no error. The button label flipped to 'Hide Brain Settings' so the expansion itself worked; the content is simply a permanent loading state.
expected: Either do not offer Brain Settings when PHD2 is disconnected, or resolve the load to an explicit 'Connect PHD2 to read its brain parameters'.
repro: 1. Guiding with PHD2 not running. 2. Press 'Brain Settings'. 3. Wait 20+ s and screenshot.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-75-brain.png (immediately after expanding) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-brain.png (20 s later - unchanged shimmer rows)
proposed_fix: Give the brain-params fetch a timeout and an error state, and render the disconnected case as text rather than as an indefinite skeleton.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: with PHD2 disconnected I pressed 'Brain Settings', the label flipped to 'Hide Brain Settings' and six grey shimmer rows appeared; they were still shimmering on re-capture several minutes later, with no values, no message and no error. The cause is exact: BrainParamsNotifier (guiding_provider/brain_and_calibration.dart:16-53) is constructed in `AsyncValue.loading()` and only calls fetch() when the guider is connected AND deviceId == 'phd2_guider'; the disconnect listener also resets it to loading. So with PHD2 absent the provider can never leave `loading`, and desktop_sections.dart:868-889 renders `loading:` as six ShimmerLoading rows forever. Note the panel is not missing an error surface as implied — :891-926 has a full error state with the real message and a Retry button; it is simply unreachable because the fetch never runs. Reduced to P3: it is a misleading placeholder only reachable when PHD2 is disconnected, with no data or safety consequence.

title: Framing sidebar "Equipment" section shows an indefinite spinner for over 20 minutes on first load
what_happened: On first arrival at the Framing screen (10:34) the Equipment section rendered nothing but a CircularProgressIndicator. It was still spinning at 10:36 and at 10:38 (2.5 min), still spinning on a second visit at 10:43 (9 min), and only resolved to 'My First Rig / Camera: Simulated Camera / Telescope: 530mm f/5.0' on a third visit at 10:55 - about 21 minutes after first load. Meanwhile the FOV / Resolution / Sensor rows immediately below it were populated the whole time, so the underlying data was available; only the AsyncValue feeding the Equipment card was stuck in `loading`. The status badge beside the 'Equipment' heading also renders as an empty SizedBox while loading, so there is not even a hint that anything is pending.
expected: The Equipment summary resolves in well under a second (it is a local camera-status query against an already-connected device) or shows an explicit error.
repro: 1. Connect sim camera + mount. 2. Plan Tonight -> Framing. 3. Watch the Equipment section under the Target search box.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-82-framing3.png (spinner, 10:36), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-framing-equip.png (still a spinner at 10:38 after a 35 s wait), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-95-framing-utils.png (still spinning, 10:43), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-102-opticalcfg.png (resolved at 10:55)
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/widgets/framing_sidebar/target_and_equipment.dart:352 (loading: () => const SizedBox()) and :458-461 (loading: 60px spinner); the future comes from framing_provider/support.dart:100-104 backend.getCameraStatus
proposed_fix: Time-bound the getCameraStatus call and render an error card on timeout. Replace the empty-SizedBox loading badge with a visible 'Loading...' so a hang is not invisible.
verdict_reasoning: The symptom reproduces, but the described shape ('stuck in loading for ~21 minutes, then resolved') is wrong; it flickers. Sampling the Equipment card region ten times over ~30 s, eight samples contained nothing but a centred spinner (4 bright pixels in the content band) and two contained the resolved 'My First Rig / Camera Simulated Camera / Telescope 530mm f/5.0' (837 bright pixels) — so the card spends most of its time in the loading branch and intermittently paints the data. That also resolves what looked like a self-contradiction in the report (spinner above, populated FOV/Resolution/Sensor below): both are fed by the same framingFOVProvider via one `equipmentAsync`, but `.when(loading:)` (target_and_equipment.dart:458-461) re-enters loading on every provider re-run while the rows below read `equipmentAsync.valueOrNull` (controls_and_status.dart:20) and keep the retained value. framingFOVProvider (framing_provider/support.dart:40-104) watches framingProvider, activeEquipmentProfileProvider, cameraStateProvider and backendProvider, so camera telemetry churn re-triggers the async getCameraStatus repeatedly. The loading badge at :352 really is an empty SizedBox. Reduced to P3: the real equipment data is displayed immediately below and nothing is lost.

title: Annotations empty state tells the user to "Capture an image" after they have captured 12
what_happened: After 12 successful captures the Annotations tab reads '0/0 objects' and the empty state says 'No image annotated - Capture an image to see detected objects'. The real reason is on the same panel a few lines above ('No plate solver installed') and in the page banner ('Annotations are enabled but no catalog is installed'), but the empty state instructs the user to redo something they have already done 12 times.
expected: 'Cannot annotate: no plate solver / no catalog installed' with the same Setup action the banner already offers.
repro: 1. Take any snapshot. 2. Imaging -> Annotations tab. Read the empty-state text.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-49-annotationstab.png ('0/0 objects', 'No plate solver installed', 'No image annotated / Capture an image to see detected objects') taken after 11 frames were already in the session panel
proposed_fix: Branch the empty state on (has image) x (has solver) x (has catalog) and name the actual blocker.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by reading the code, though not reproduced on screen (my session had already run an annotate pass, so the panel showed the other branch, 'Found 0 objects' / 'No objects match filters'). The empty state branches on one variable only: `annotation == null` -> 'No image annotated' plus the subtitle 'Capture an image to see detected objects'. Nothing in that branch consults how many frames exist, whether a plate solver is installed, or whether the annotation catalog is present, so the copy is wrong for exactly the state the reporter hit (12 captures, no solver, no catalog). One file-attribution correction: the 'Capture an image to see detected objects' subtitle is at annotation_panel_parts/tab_panel.dart:911-923, not objects_panel.dart — objects_panel.dart:864-868 has the same 'No image annotated' branch but without the subtitle. Reduced to P3: it is misleading copy in a corner case, adjacent to a banner that already names the real blocker.

title: Overlays menu label wraps mid-word to "Rea / dou"
what_happened: The last item of the preview Overlays popup renders its label broken across two lines as 'Rea' / 'dou' because the trailing description 'Histogram, HFR / stars, image stats' consumes the row width. The intended label is 'Readouts' (imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:385).
expected: 'Readouts' on one line, with the description ellipsised or moved to a second line.
repro: 1. Imaging -> Overlays dropdown. 2. Look at the bottom row.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-61-overlays.png (row reads 'Rea'/'dou' with the description to its right)
proposed_fix: Wrap the label in Flexible with softWrap:false + TextOverflow.ellipsis, or give the description its own line.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim in my own instance: I opened the preview Overlays popup and the last row renders its label broken across two lines as 'Rea' / 'dou' with the description 'Histogram, HFR / stars, image stats' to its right (evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vfy-04-overlays.png). Intended label 'Readouts' at imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:385. P3 is right.

title: Annotation panel's plate-solver warning is hard-clipped at the panel edge with no ellipsis
what_happened: The 'No plate solver installed' card inside the Annotations tab renders its second line as 'Optional: install ASTAP or set its path in Settings to label ob' and is cut off flat at the panel border - no ellipsis, no wrap, the sentence just ends mid-word.
expected: The text wraps to a third line (there is vertical room) or ellipsises.
repro: 1. Imaging -> Annotations tab. 2. Read the warning card in the right panel.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-49-annotationstab.png (right-panel card, second line clipped at the panel edge)
proposed_fix: Wrap the Text in Expanded/Flexible with softWrap: true.
verdict_reasoning: I could not put my instance into the solverMissing state (annotation had already run there), so I verified this two other ways. The cited evidence renders as described: cropping /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-49-annotationstab.png at the right panel shows '...plate solver installed' with the second line '...onal: install ASTAP or set its path in Settings to label ob' cut flat at the panel border, mid-word, with no ellipsis. And the layout explains it: status_widgets.dart:127-157 builds Row(mainAxisSize.min) -> icon -> Column(mainAxisSize.min) of Texts with no Flexible/Expanded anywhere, so the secondary Text is laid out at its unconstrained intrinsic width; its maxLines:2 + TextOverflow.ellipsis (:155-156) can never fire because the text never needs to wrap, and the overflowing Row is simply clipped by the panel. P3 is right.

title: Onboarding promises target/date subfolders; every frame lands flat in the chosen directory
what_happened: The onboarding capture-folder step states 'Sessions will be organized into target/date subfolders under this directory.' I chose /tmp. All 11 frames were written directly to /tmp as Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_NNNN.fits with no subfolder of any kind, and captured_images.file_path confirms the flat paths.
expected: Either honour the promise for Imaging-screen captures too, or scope the copy to say it applies to sequencer runs only.
repro: 1. Onboarding -> capture folder step, read the caption, pick /tmp. 2. Imaging -> Snapshot. 3. `ls /tmp/*.fits` - flat.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-13-folder.png (the caption), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-18-folderdone.png (/tmp selected, 'Folder is writable'), `ls -lat /tmp/*.fits` -> 11 files directly in /tmp, sqlite file_path = /tmp/Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0001.fits
proposed_fix: Apply the same target/date folder builder the sequencer uses to manual captures, or fix the onboarding sentence.
verdict_reasoning: Both halves check out. The copy exists verbatim at onboarding/steps/capture_dir_step.dart:312: 'Sessions will be organized into target/date subfolders under this directory.' The shipped default naming pattern is flat: database/database/default_settings.dart:21 sets 'file_naming_pattern' to $TARGET_$FILTER_$DATE_$SEQ (also the default in app_settings_state.dart:485), and my profile's DB confirms that value is what is actually stored. Result: all 22 frames landed directly in /tmp/ns-verify-caps as Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_NNNN.fits with captured_images.file_path flat. Worth noting the subfolder machinery exists and works — file_paths.dart:5-23 documents the pattern as a /-separated path and the NamingPattern model default (naming_and_autofocus.dart:10) is $TARGET/$FRAMETYPE/... — the shipped settings default just overrides it with a flat one. P3 is right.

title: FITS omits XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ (and OBJECT) although onboarding collects pixel size and uses it to compute image scale
what_happened: Onboarding's optical-train step asks for 'Camera pixel size' (I entered 3.76 um) and immediately shows 'Image scale 1.46 arcsec/px' computed from it, and the Framing OPTICAL CONFIG card displays '(3.76um)'. Yet every written FITS has FOCALLEN and APTDIA but no XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ and no OBJECT. The Dart header builder hard-codes `pixelSizeX: null, pixelSizeY: null` with the comment 'Pixel size not stored in profile yet', which is no longer true. Without XPIXSZ many downstream tools (ASTAP blind solve hints, PixInsight, AstroBin) cannot derive plate scale from the file alone.
expected: XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ written from the profile pixel size; OBJECT written when a target is known.
repro: 1. Onboard entering pixel size 3.76. 2. Imaging -> Snapshot. 3. Dump the FITS header.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-11-optrain-filled.png (pixel size 3.76, image scale 1.46 arcsec/px), header dump listing SIMPLE..AIRMASS..END with no XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ/OBJECT
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service/persistence.dart:73-74 ('pixelSizeX: null, // Pixel size not stored in profile yet')
proposed_fix: Read pixel size from the active profile (or the camera status) and pass it through; delete the stale comment.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed: dumping every FITS in /tmp/ns-verify-caps shows FOCALLEN=530.0 present and no XPIXSZ, no YPIXSZ, no OBJECT card in any of the 22 files, and persistence.dart:73-74 passes `pixelSizeX: null, pixelSizeY: null` with the comment 'Pixel size not stored in profile yet'. The Rust writer supports the keywords (api/imaging.rs:3584/3588, 3720/3724, 4021/4025 write XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ scaled by binning), so only the Dart caller is dropping them. Two corrections to the supporting argument. (1) 'the comment is no longer true' is itself wrong — the equipment_profiles table has no pixel-size column (only camera_id/camera_name) and CameraStateSnapshot carries no pixel size either; the value is reachable, but only via backend.getCameraStatus, the same call the Framing provider makes (support.dart:102-107, pixel_size_x=3.76). (2) The missing OBJECT is not a bug in this case: persistence.dart:47 passes `objectName: targetName`, which is null for a manual capture with no session target. P3 is right.
